This mod has overrides of non-NPC records.
NPC2 can handle these using the default option in the settings menu, or on a per-mod basis configured here.

IMPORTANT: Just because the plugin has overrides doesn't mean these overrides need to be handled. In most cases, non-NPC overrides are safe to ignore,

modsOverrideHandlingTooltip:
Controls what happens if plugins in this mod override records from another mod (other than the direct NPC records).

Default: Use the default setting from the Settings Tab.
Ignore: Do not look for overridden records. Conflict patching will be fully taken care of by you.
Include: Incorporate the overridden records into the output (as whole records in Default mode, or deltas in EasyNPC mode).
Include as New: Copy the overrides as new records. Avoids conflicts if multiple appearance mods override the same records.
modsWigHandlingTooltip:
This mod ships wigs: hair-slot wig armors in its Default Outfits, and/or hair meshes carried directly in an NPC's skin (worn armor — the High Poly NPC Overhaul pattern). Controls how they are handled during patching — and how mugshots and the 3D preview depict the NPC. Antlers are controlled separately.

Default: Use the default setting from the Settings tab.
Forward To Skin: transfer an outfit wig into the NPC's skin (WornArmor) so it shows regardless of the outfit worn (falls back to Forward To Outfit if the appearance plugin assigns no WornArmor). A skin-carried wig is already in this state and is left as-is.
Forward To Outfit: duplicate the outfit the NPC actually wears in game and add the wig to the duplicate (no change if it already contains the wig). A skin-carried wig is moved into that outfit as a generated wig armor.
Convert To Headparts (EXPERIMENTAL): discard the wig armor and make the wig the NPC's hair — generated head part records + the wig mesh baked into the FaceGen file (HDT-SMP preserved; helmets hide it like normal hair). Works for outfit wigs AND skin-carried wigs (the 3D preview's "Set Wig Meshes" button corrects which skin meshes count as wigs). An outfit wig falls back to Forward To Skin per NPC when the bake would be unsafe; a skin-carried wig is left as-is instead.
Leave As Is: wigs are treated like any other outfit/skin element — an outfit wig is forwarded only if Include Outfits is selected; a skin-carried wig stays in the skin.
modsWigColorTooltip:
Only applies when this mod's Wig Handling Mode resolves to Convert To Headparts. Many wig meshes carry a near-black placeholder hair color and rely on RaceMenu to recolor them in game (RaceMenu automatically tints worn hair-slot items — that is why High Poly NPC Overhaul gives every NPC black hair until RaceMenu is installed). A wig baked into the FaceGen file is no longer a worn item, so RaceMenu stops recoloring it and the placeholder sticks. This bakes the NPC's own hair color in instead.

Default: Use the default setting from the Settings tab.
Auto: recolor only wigs carrying a placeholder tint; leave wigs whose textures are already colored by their author alone.
Always use NPC's hair color: recolor every converted wig, exactly as RaceMenu would have done to the original worn wig.
Keep the wig's own color: never touch the wig's baked hair color.
modsAntlerHandlingTooltip:
This mod ships antlers (in an outfit, baked into the worn armor, or as a keyword-detected FaceGen head part). Controls how they are handled during patching — and how mugshots and the 3D preview depict the NPC.

Default: Use the default setting from the Settings tab.
Forward To Skin: transfer the antler into the NPC's skin (WornArmor) so it shows regardless of the outfit worn. Falls back to Forward To Outfit if the appearance plugin assigns no WornArmor.
Forward To Outfit: duplicate the outfit the NPC actually wears in game and add the antler to the duplicate.
Remove: keep the antler OFF the NPC entirely — stripped from a forwarded outfit, from the worn armor, and from the FaceGen. An outfit the load order owns (not forwarded) can't be reached.
Leave As Is: the antler is treated like any other outfit element — forwarded only if Include Outfits is selected.
modsTemplateNpcsTooltip:
Some of this mod's NPCs copy their face from another NPC instead of having one of their own (the NPCs tab marks them with a Template icon). Controls what a selection from this mod does for those NPCs.

Default: Use the default setting from the Settings tab.
Use the template's appearance: they keep showing the other NPC's face, and any appearance you pick for them is ignored.
Give each NPC its own copy: your choice is applied to each of them individually, so NPCs that share a template can look different. Adds one copy of the face files per NPC. NPCs whose face the game picks at random from a levelled list keep inheriting either way.
modsTraversalDepthTooltip:
Controls how many layers deep the patcher will search for overridden records between finding relevant records.

This is not a total depth limit. The count resets every time a record from this mod is found, so a continuous chain of the mod's records is always followed all the way down.

The default of 2 is what lets the search cross one unrelated record (e.g. a vanilla outfit) to reach the mod's edits below it. Higher values may find more obscure overrides but will significantly increase patching time.

Leave blank to use the default. Set to 1 to only check direct dependencies; 0 disables the search entirely.
modsOverrideRootsTooltip:
Choose which fields of an NPC record the search for this mod's overridden records may start from.

A selected field is followed as deep as it goes, through any kind of record. This does not limit which record types can be merged in — only where the search begins. Defaults to the fields that carry appearance.
settingsDefaultOverrideRootsTooltip:
The default choice of which NPC-record fields the search for a mod's overridden records may start from. Individual mods can override this from their own "Override Roots" button.

A selected field is followed as deep as it goes, through any kind of record. This does not limit which record types can be merged in — only where the search begins.

Some NPCs copy their face from another NPC instead of having one of their own (the NPC menu marks them with a Template icon).

Use the template's appearance (default): they keep showing the other NPC's face, and any appearance you pick for them is ignored.

Give each NPC its own copy: your choice is applied to each of them individually, so NPCs that share a template can look different. Adds one copy of the face files per NPC. NPCs whose face the game picks at random from a levelled list keep inheriting either way.
settingsWigHandlingTooltip:
How detected wigs are handled during patching. Wigs come from two places: hair-slot wig armors in a mod's Default Outfits, and hair meshes carried directly in an NPC's skin (worn armor — the High Poly NPC Overhaul pattern). Applies in Create and Patch mode and in SkyPatcher mode; individual mods can override this in the Mods menu when a wig is detected. Antlers are controlled separately (below).

Forward To Skin: an outfit wig becomes part of the NPC's skin (WornArmor), so it shows no matter what outfit the NPC wears (falls back to Forward To Outfit if the appearance plugin assigns no WornArmor). A skin-carried wig is already in this state and is left as-is.

Forward To Outfit: the outfit the NPC actually wears in game is duplicated and the wig added to the duplicate (no change if it already contains the wig). A skin-carried wig is moved into that outfit as a generated wig armor.

Convert To Headparts (EXPERIMENTAL): the wig armor is discarded entirely and the wig becomes the NPC's hair — new head part records are generated and the wig mesh is baked into the FaceGen file (HDT-SMP physics is preserved). Survives outfit changes and helmets hide it like normal hair. Works for outfit wigs AND skin-carried wigs (the 3D preview's "Set Wig Meshes" button corrects which skin meshes count as wigs). An outfit wig falls back to Forward To Skin per NPC when the bake would be unsafe (e.g. the appearance mod ships no baked hair to replace); a skin-carried wig is left as-is instead.

Leave As Is: wigs are treated like any other outfit/skin element — an outfit wig is forwarded only if Include Outfits is selected; a skin-carried wig stays in the skin.
settingsWigColorTooltip:
Only applies to wigs handled with Convert To Headparts. Many wig meshes are authored with a near-black placeholder hair color because they expect RaceMenu to recolor them in game (RaceMenu automatically tints worn hair-slot items — it is why some mods, notably High Poly NPC Overhaul, give every NPC black hair until RaceMenu is installed). Once a wig is baked into the FaceGen file it is no longer a worn item, so RaceMenu stops recoloring it and the placeholder becomes permanent. This setting bakes the NPC's own hair color in instead, which is what the Creation Kit does for normal hair.

Auto: recolor only wigs that carry a placeholder tint. Wigs whose textures are already colored by their author (a neutral white tint) are left alone. The default, and the safe choice.

Always: recolor every converted wig with the NPC's hair color, exactly as RaceMenu would have done to the original worn wig.

Never: leave the wig's baked hair color untouched.
settingsWigScopeTooltip:
How broadly a skin-carried hair mesh you manually mark as a wig — or as NOT a wig — (via the 3D preview's "Set Wig Meshes" button) applies. This controls scope only — a wig is still converted only when its mod's Wig Handling Mode is Convert To Head Parts.

All NPCs (any mod): apply the designation to that mesh's EditorID wherever it appears (the default).

Same mod only: apply it only in the mod it was designated in.

Specific NPC(s) only: apply it only on the NPC(s) it was designated on.
settingsAntlerHandlingTooltip:
How detected antler armors/head parts are handled during patching. Applies in Create and Patch mode and in SkyPatcher mode; individual mods can override this in the Mods menu when an antler is detected.

Forward To Skin: the antler becomes part of the NPC's skin (WornArmor), so it shows no matter what outfit the NPC wears. Falls back to Forward To Outfit if the appearance plugin assigns no WornArmor. (The pre-split default — leave this to keep existing behavior.)

Forward To Outfit: the outfit the NPC actually wears in game is duplicated and the antler added to the duplicate.

Remove: keep the antler OFF the NPC entirely — stripped from a forwarded outfit, from the worn armor, and from the FaceGen (keyword-detected antler head parts). Antlers baked into an outfit the load order owns (not forwarded) can't be reached.

Leave As Is: the antler is treated like any other outfit element — forwarded only if Include Outfits is selected.
settingsAntlerScopeTooltip:
How broadly a head part you manually designate as an antler (via the 3D preview's "Set Antler Head Parts" button) is blocked. This controls scope only — a head part is still removed only when its mod's Antler Handling Mode is Remove.

All NPCs (any mod): block that head part's EditorID wherever it appears (the default).

Same mod only: block it only in the mod it was designated in.

Specific NPC(s) only: block it only on the NPC(s) it was designated on, regardless of which mod supplies that NPC's appearance.
settingsRuntimeOutfitTooltip:
Some NPCs have their outfit assigned at runtime by SkyPatcher or SPID rather than by a plugin record. For those NPCs a wig or antler forwarded to the outfit would be wiped out in game, because the distributor overwrites the outfit the patch assigned.

With this on, the patcher writes its own config for exactly those NPCs — a SkyPatcher entry when a SkyPatcher config contests the outfit, a generated *_DISTR.ini when a SPID config does — pointing at the duplicated outfit that carries the wig/antler, so it survives. Nothing is written for NPCs whose outfit no distributor touches.

With this off, those NPCs are only warned about in the patch log and the forwarded wig/antler will most likely not appear in game.

helpOverrideHandlingMode:
Override Handling Mode:

This setting determines how the default behavior for how the patcher handles mods that override/modify non-appearance records from the base game or other mods.

IMPORANT: Handling overrides makes patching take longer, and is only needed in very rare cases. You almost certainly should leave the default behavior as Ignore.

Options:

- Ignore:
  - The overriden records will be left as-is. If there are conflicts, it'll be up to you to patch them yourself.
  - The output plugin will be mastered to the mods providing the records being overridden.

- Include:
  - The overriden records will be copied into the output plugin.
  - In Create And Patch mode, only the changed aspects of the record will be applied.
  - The output plugin will still be mastered to the mods providing the records being overridden.

- Include As New:
  - The overridden records will be added to the output plugin as new records.
  - This mode may be appropriate if you have two Appearance Mods overriding the same record in different ways, which would make them incompatible with each other otherwise.

You can edit this file in NotePad or add the keyword manually to any Mods that aren't in the default list using the Set Keywords button.

You can also create additional files (e.g., CotR_Plugins_Custom.txt) to add more plugins without modifying the original file, making your changes update-safe.

msg_217SplitMessage:
Starting in 2.1.7, FaceFinder downloads and auto-generated mugshots live in their own dedicated folders instead of sharing the curated Mugshots Folder you set up. This lets you switch between curated, FaceFinder, and auto-generated images per NPC without those sources overwriting each other.

Defaults:
  • FaceFinder cache → <install dir>\FaceFinder Cache
  • Auto-generated   → <install dir>\AutoGen Mugshots
  • Curated mugshots stay where you set them.

Would you like NPC2 to move your existing FaceFinder and auto-generated mugshots out of the curated folder into these new locations now? (Recommended)

msg_223FilterIntro1: 2.2.3 changed how N.P.C.2 decides which NPCs have a customizable face. It now reads the Race record's "FaceGen Head" flag (the game's own signal for whether an actor gets a face) instead of the ActorTypeNPC keyword, and it reads it from the end of an NPC's template chain rather than from the NPC's own record.
msg_223FilterIntro2: This adds NPCs that were previously excluded by mistake (Miraak, for example). It also removes NPCs that turned out to have no face at all - typically automatons, skeletons and other monsters whose mod authors tagged them as people so they would behave correctly in combat and dialogue.

whichModToScan:
Which mod to scan. ALL scans every eligible appearance mod.
Type to search the list — Scan then covers the exact pick, or every mod matching the typed text.
scanTheTargetedAppearance: Scan the targeted appearance mods for missing assets (ALL = every installed appearance mod). Mods that haven't changed since the last scan are skipped (cached).
scanTheTargetedMods: Scan the targeted mods from scratch, ignoring cached results.
exportAllDetectedIssues: Export all detected issues to a CSV file.
showOnlyModsWith:
Show only mods with an affected NPC whose name or FormKey matches.
Ctrl+Shift+C clears all search filters
showOnlyModsAnd: Show only mods (and NPC tiles) with this kind of issue
ifUncheckedModsAnd: If unchecked, mods and NPCs whose only problems are outfit/headgear-related are hidden, leaving just face and body defects.
issuesAreVisiblyBroken: Issues are visibly broken in game right now — dark faces, invisible or untextured meshes, missing required mods.
warningsRenderFineToday: Warnings render fine today but can break under realistic conditions — assets supplied by another installed mod that must stay activated, defects the ghost effect currently hides, weight-pair files this NPC's weight happens not to need.
notesAreEngineInert: Notes are engine-inert or imperceptible findings — secondary texture maps (specular, environment, subsurface) that even vanilla meshes reference without shipping, or records this mod can never forward into a patch.
showIssuesYouHave: Show issues you have ignored (right-click a results row to ignore/unignore). Ignored issues are excluded from counts, badges and CSV export while hidden.
collapseTheResultsTable: Collapse the results table to one row per distinct problem with an NPC count — shared body/head meshes repeat the same missing file across many NPCs. Clicking a mugshot still shows that NPC's individual rows.
showThisModIn: Show this mod in the Mods tab
showOnlyThisIssue: Show only this issue type (click again to show all)
modHasChangedSince: ⚠ Mod has changed since this scan — results may be outdated
ignoreThisFileForMod: Ignore this file for this mod (all NPCs)
ignoreThisFileInAllMods: Ignore this file in ALL mods
keepTheCurrentZoom: Keep the current zoom level instead of auto-fitting
copyTheClassicIndented: Copy the classic indented report (grouped by master, then record).
templatedNpcsCopyTheir: Templated NPCs copy their appearance from another NPC, so an unplaced one simply keeps its template's look. Untick to hide their rows and surface the NPCs with more fixable issues.
unloadedNpcsBaseNpc: Unloaded NPCs ('Base NPC not found in load order') have their defining plugin missing or disabled, so the run skipped them. Untick to hide their rows.

Costs a render per tile each time an NPC is selected. Individual tiles can always be switched via right-click > Make Live Tile, regardless of this setting.
deleteTileImageTooltip: Delete the image currently shown on this tile and fall back to the next available mugshot source.

liveTileViewportExplanation: Live Tile turns this mugshot into a miniature 3D viewport (left-drag to rotate, middle-drag to move, wheel to zoom), framed like the auto-generated mugshot. Make Mugshot turns it back into a static image.
renderNowTooltip: Render this appearance now with the built-in 3D renderer, replacing any auto-generated mugshot it already has. Works whether or not Auto-Generate missing mugshots is switched on.

toggleLiveTileTooltip: Toggle Live Tile mode for the checked mugshots (Requires 1+ selected). 3D turns them into embedded 3D viewports; 2D turns them back into static mugshots. On a mixed selection the button applies the state shown.
ungreyLiveTileExplanation: Un-greys the 'Live Tile' source above. Place it first to always get live 3D tiles, or last as a fallback when no image exists.
dataFolderAssetsIconExplanation: When on (default), a mugshot that pulled non-vanilla assets from your data folder — because they were not found in the mod's Corresponding Mod Folders — shows the data-folder-assets icon, recorded in the PNG so it survives restarts. These assets come from some other installed mod: it must stay activated, or be added to this mod's Corresponding Mod Folders, for the NPC to look right in game. Informational only — the render itself is correct. Unchecking hides the icon and re-renders the affected mugshots once so their recorded state is cleared.
